A_target.statement:
Let $\mathbf A$ be a [[Definition:Square Matrix|square matrix]] with strictly positive entries.
Then there exist $\mathbf v$ with all entries positive and $\lambda > 0$ such that:
:$\mathbf A \mathbf v = \lambda \mathbf v$

B_source.statement:
Let $K \subseteq \R^n$ be [[Definition:Compact Space|compact]] and [[Definition:Convex Set (Vector Space)|convex]], and $f: K \to K$ [[Definition:Continuous Mapping|continuous]].
Then there exists $x \in K$ with $\map f x = x$.

substitutions.the compact convex set K: the standard simplex of nonnegative vectors summing to one

object_map.reformulation: The eigenvector equation is scale-invariant, so it must be reformulated on the projective quotient represented by the simplex before it becomes a genuine self-map.

validity_conditions: A must have nonnegative entries so the simplex is preserved
Ax must be nonzero on the simplex for the normalization to be defined, guaranteed by strict positivity
strict positivity is what upgrades existence to a strictly positive eigenvector and gives uniqueness
proof_plan: Let $\Delta = \set {\mathbf x \in \R^n_{\ge 0}: \sum_i x_i = 1}$ be the [[Definition:Standard Simplex|standard simplex]], which is compact and convex.

Define:
:$\map g {\mathbf x} = \dfrac {\mathbf A \mathbf x} {\norm {\mathbf A \mathbf x}_1}$

For $\mathbf x \in \Delta$, $\mathbf A \mathbf x$ has non-negative entries and is non-zero, so $\norm {\mathbf A \mathbf x}_1 > 0$.
Hence $g$ is continuous and maps $\Delta$ into itself.

By the [[Brouwer Fixed Point Theorem]], there exists $\mathbf v \in \Delta$ with:
:$\dfrac {\mathbf A \mathbf v} {\norm {\mathbf A \mathbf v}_1} = \mathbf v$

Let $\lambda = \norm {\mathbf A \mathbf v}_1 > 0$.
Then $\mathbf A \mathbf v = \lambda \mathbf v$.
As $\mathbf A$ has strictly positive entries and $\mathbf v \ne \mathbf 0$, every entry of $\mathbf A \mathbf v$ is positive, so every entry of $\mathbf v$ is positive.
This is the [[Perron-Frobenius Theorem]] for positive matrices.
{{qed}}
